blocks.text: Practice MCQs for the whole of Chapter 7 (Structural and Computational Biology), arranged by the chapter's sections. Each question has one correct answer with a short explanation; numerical questions show the working.

blocks.prompt: 1 Structural biology deals with the study of macromolecules such as proteins and nucleic acids at the level of their:
blocks.explanation: Structural biology studies the 3D structures of macromolecules (proteins and nucleic acids) at atomic levels (7.1).

book_ref.quote: Structural biology deals with the study of three dimensional (3D) structures of macromolecules

blocks.prompt: 2 Besides the structure of a biomolecule, structural biology gives detailed information about its:

options.text: functions, dynamics and interaction with ligands

blocks.explanation: Structural biology gives detailed information about a biomolecule's structure, functions, dynamics and interaction with ligands and other macromolecules (7.1).

book_ref.quote: its functions, dynamics and interaction with ligands and other macromolecules

blocks.prompt: 3 In the enzyme HIV-1 reverse transcriptase, the domain that synthesizes DNA is the:
blocks.explanation: Structural studies of HIV-1 reverse transcriptase identified its polymerase domain, which synthesizes DNA (7.1).

book_ref.quote: polymerase domain (which synthesizes DNA)

blocks.prompt: 4 The RNase H domain of HIV-1 reverse transcriptase:

options.text: breaks down the RNA strand of RNA-DNA hybrids
binds to the human receptor protein

blocks.explanation: The RNase H domain breaks down the RNA strand of RNA-DNA hybrids; the polymerase domain synthesizes DNA (7.1).

book_ref.quote: which breaks down the RNA strand of RNA-DNA hybrids

blocks.prompt: 5 Knowing the location and structure of the domains of HIV-1 reverse transcriptase has helped in:

options.text: designing antiviral drugs that specifically target them

blocks.explanation: Knowledge of these domains helped in designing antiviral drugs that specifically target them (7.1).

book_ref.quote: Knowing the location and structure of these domains has helped in the design of antiviral drugs

blocks.prompt: 6 The well-defined active site of serine proteases is responsible for:
blocks.explanation: The structure of serine proteases shows a well-defined active site that breaks down peptide bonds (7.1).

book_ref.quote: the structure of serine proteases reveals its well-defined active site

blocks.prompt: 7 The places on a disease-causing molecule where a drug can work, usually proteins, are called:
blocks.explanation: Structural biology finds the places on a disease-causing molecule where a drug can work; these, usually proteins, are drug targets (7.1).

book_ref.quote: These places are usually proteins and are called drug targets

blocks.prompt: 8 In COVID-19, the protein of SARS-CoV-2 identified as a drug target because it helps the virus enter human cells is the:
blocks.explanation: The spike protein helps the virus enter human cells; knowing its 3D structure, scientists made it a drug target and designed vaccines and medicines that block it (7.1).

book_ref.quote: This protein helps the virus to enter human cells

blocks.prompt: 9 Vaccines and medicines designed against the spike protein of the coronavirus work by:

options.text: blocking the spike protein so the virus cannot infect more cells

blocks.explanation: Vaccines and medicines block the spike protein, preventing the virus from infecting more cells (7.1).

book_ref.quote: they designed vaccines and medicines that block the spike protein

blocks.prompt: 10 The way pathogens such as viruses or bacteria interact with the host's body cells is called:
blocks.explanation: Understanding how pathogens interact with host cells is called host–pathogen interaction; structural biology studies the 3D structures of both proteins (7.1).

book_ref.quote: This is called host–pathogen interaction

blocks.prompt: 11 A drug that binds with the receptor protein on human cells blocks a virus by:

options.text: inhibiting the interaction of the virus with the receptor, blocking its entry
changing the virus into a bacterium

blocks.explanation: Such a drug inhibits the virus-receptor interaction and consequently blocks the entry of the virus into host cells (7.1).

book_ref.quote: Such drug inhibits the interaction of the virus with the receptor

blocks.prompt: 12 Which of the following diseases originates due to incorrect folding of proteins?
blocks.explanation: Cystic fibrosis, Parkinson's disease and Alzheimer's disease originate due to incorrect folding of proteins (the book misspells these names) (7.1).

book_ref.quote: originate due to incorrect folding of proteins

blocks.prompt: 13 In the study of protein misfolding, structural biology provides an understanding of:

options.text: intricate folding pathways and how misfolding leads to disease

blocks.explanation: Structural biology explains intricate folding pathways and how misfolding leads to diseases (7.1).

book_ref.quote: Structural biology provides understanding of intricate folding pathways

blocks.prompt: 14 William Henry Bragg and William Lawrence Bragg, who developed X-ray crystallography, were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in:
blocks.explanation: X-ray crystallography was developed by the Braggs, who received the 1915 Nobel Prize in Physics (7.2).

book_ref.quote: They were awarded 1915 Nobel Prize in Physics for their work

blocks.prompt: 15 In X-ray crystallography, the X-ray beam striking a crystal is:

options.text: diffracted in specific directions by the atoms and molecules of the crystal

blocks.explanation: When the X-ray beam strikes a crystal, its atoms and molecules diffract the beam in specific directions (7.2).

book_ref.quote: atoms and molecules in the crystals diffract the x-rays beam in specific directions

blocks.prompt: 16 A 3D picture of electron density within the crystal is produced from the diffracted beams':
blocks.explanation: From the angles and intensities of diffracted beams a 3D picture of electron density is produced and used to build the molecule's 3D structure (7.2).

book_ref.quote: From the angles and intensities of diffracted beams

blocks.prompt: 17 Since its development, X-ray crystallography has been used to analyse:

options.text: minerals, salts, metals, proteins, nucleic acids and vitamins

blocks.explanation: It has analysed diverse substances including minerals, salts, metals, proteins, carbohydrates, nucleic acids and vitamins (7.2).

book_ref.quote: minerals, salts, metals, proteins, carbohydrates, nucleic acids and vitamins

blocks.prompt: 18 Protein crystals are needed in X-ray crystallography because they:

options.text: arrange protein molecules in a regular, repeating pattern
make the protein soluble in water

blocks.explanation: Crystals arrange protein molecules in a regular, repeating pattern, which is important for a clear image during the X-ray process (7.2).

book_ref.quote: Crystals are needed because they arrange protein molecules in a regular, repeating pattern

blocks.prompt: 19 Protein crystallization often requires careful control of:
blocks.explanation: Making crystals can take hours, days or even weeks and needs careful control of temperature, pH and salt concentration (7.2).

book_ref.quote: It often requires careful control of temperature, pH, and salt concentration

blocks.prompt: 20 The process of making protein crystals can take:
blocks.explanation: Scientists slowly mix the protein with special solutions; the process can take hours, days or even weeks (7.2).

book_ref.quote: This process can take hours, days, or even weeks

blocks.prompt: 21 The diffraction pattern created on the detectors in X-ray crystallography is:
blocks.explanation: The crystal is mounted on the X-ray machine and bombarded at various angles; the diffracted beam creates a diffraction pattern, a series of spots, on the detectors (7.2).

book_ref.quote: a diffraction pattern (which is a series of spots) is created on the detectors

blocks.prompt: 22 In X-ray crystallography, the diffraction pattern is used to make a:
blocks.explanation: The angles and intensities of the spots carry information on the arrangement of atoms; the diffraction pattern is used to make a density map (7.2).

book_ref.quote: Diffraction pattern is used to make a density map

blocks.prompt: 23 In the last step of protein structure determination by X-ray crystallography, the data are:

options.text: analysed mathematically by computational programs to give the 3D structure

blocks.explanation: The data are analysed mathematically with computational programs; these calculations transform the data into the 3D structure of the protein (7.2).

book_ref.quote: These calculations transform data into the 3D structure of protein

blocks.prompt: 24 Computational biology integrates knowledge from:

options.text: biology, computer science, mathematics and statistics

blocks.explanation: Computational biology is interdisciplinary: it integrates biology, computer science, mathematics and statistics to analyse biological data (7.3).

book_ref.quote: It integrates knowledge from biology, computer science, mathematics, and statistics

blocks.prompt: 25 The importance of computational biology lies in its ability to:

options.text: handle large datasets, uncover hidden patterns and generate predictive models
observe living cells under a light microscope

blocks.explanation: Computational biology can handle large datasets, uncover hidden patterns and generate predictive models leading to new insights (7.3).

book_ref.quote: its ability to handle large datasets, uncover hidden patterns, and generate predictive models

blocks.prompt: 26 A genome is:

options.text: the entire set of proteins of an organism
the complete set of DNA within a single cell of an organism

blocks.explanation: Genomics studies genomes, the complete set of DNA within a single cell of an organism (7.3).

book_ref.quote: which are the complete set of DNA within a single cell of an organism

blocks.prompt: 27 The entire set of proteins produced by an organism is called its:
blocks.explanation: Proteomics, the large-scale study of proteins, aims to map the proteome, the entire set of proteins of an organism (7.3).

book_ref.quote: Proteomics aims to map the entire set of proteins (the proteome) produced by an organism

blocks.prompt: 28 The application of computer technology to store, retrieve and analyse DNA, RNA and protein sequences is:
blocks.explanation: Bioinformatics applies computer technology to manage and analyse biological data, e.g. DNA, RNA and protein sequences (7.3).

book_ref.quote: the application of computer technology to manage and analyze biological data

blocks.prompt: 29 Computational biology accelerates drug discovery by:

options.text: predicting how drugs interact with proteins and other molecules

blocks.explanation: It identifies potential drug targets, simulates drug effects and speeds discovery by predicting how drugs interact with proteins (7.3).

book_ref.quote: It accelerates the drug discovery process by predicting how drugs interact with proteins

blocks.prompt: 30 By identifying genetic variations associated with diseases, computational biology can lead to:
blocks.explanation: In genetic research, analysing DNA sequences finds disease-linked variations, explaining the genetic basis of disease and leading to personalized medicine (7.3).

book_ref.quote: can lead to the development of personalized medicine

blocks.prompt: 31 In evolutionary biology, computational tools compare genetic information across species to:
blocks.explanation: Computational tools compare genetic information across species to reconstruct evolutionary relationships and understand evolution (7.3).

book_ref.quote: helping to reconstruct evolutionary relationships

blocks.prompt: 32 GenBank is a comprehensive public database of:
blocks.explanation: GenBank is a public database of nucleotide sequences with bibliographic and biological annotations (7.3).

book_ref.quote: It is a comprehensive public database of nucleotide sequences

blocks.prompt: 33 The database that provides 3D structural data of large biological molecules such as proteins and nucleic acids is:
blocks.explanation: The Protein Data Bank (PDB) provides 3D structural data of large biological molecules and helps in drug design (7.3).

book_ref.quote: This database provides 3D structural data of large biological molecules

blocks.prompt: 34 Ensembl is a:
blocks.explanation: Ensembl is a genome browser giving genome sequences, gene models and comparative genomics for various species (7.3).

book_ref.quote: It is a genome browser providing information on genome sequences

blocks.prompt: 35 BLAST stands for:

options.text: Biological Linear Analysis of Sequence Types
Bioinformatics Library of All Sequence Tools

blocks.explanation: BLAST (Basic Local Alignment Search Tool) compares primary biological sequences such as amino-acid or nucleotide sequences (7.3).

book_ref.quote: BLAST (Basic Local Alignment Search Tool)

blocks.prompt: 36 BLAST is used to:

options.text: identify homologous sequences and predict functions of unknown genes

blocks.explanation: BLAST helps identify homologous sequences, predict functions of unknown genes and study evolutionary relationships (7.3).

book_ref.quote: It helps identify homologous sequences, predict functions of unknown genes

blocks.prompt: 37 The sequence alignment tool that compares a query sequence to a database of sequences to find regions of similarity is:
blocks.explanation: FASTA compares a query sequence with a database of sequences to find regions of similarity; it searches protein and nucleotide databases (7.3).

book_ref.quote: compares a query sequence to a database of sequences to find regions of similarity

blocks.prompt: 38 Similarity between DNA, RNA or protein sequences due to shared ancestry is called:
blocks.explanation: Sequence homology is the similarity between DNA, RNA or protein sequences due to shared ancestry (7.4).

book_ref.quote: Sequence homology refers to the similarity between DNA, RNA, or protein sequences due to shared ancestry

blocks.prompt: 39 Homologous sequences in different species that originated from a common ancestral gene during speciation are:
blocks.explanation: Orthologs are sequences in different species from a common ancestral gene during speciation; they often keep the same function (7.4).

book_ref.quote: Sequences in different species that originated from a common ancestral gene during speciation

blocks.prompt: 40 Paralogs are sequences:

options.text: in different species formed during speciation
of unrelated proteins with similar shapes
within the same species that originated from gene duplication

blocks.explanation: Paralogs are sequences within the same species that came from gene duplication; they can evolve new functions (7.4).

book_ref.quote: Sequences within the same species that originated from gene duplication

blocks.prompt: 41 Which statement about homologous sequences is correct?

options.text: Orthologs often retain the same function, while paralogs can evolve new functions
Paralogs are always found in different species
Orthologs arise only from gene duplication
Homologous sequences have no common ancestor

blocks.explanation: Orthologs often retain the same function across species; paralogs, though from the same ancestral gene, can evolve new functions (7.4).

book_ref.quote: Orthologs often retain the same function across species

blocks.prompt: 42 If an unknown gene is homologous to a gene with a known function, the unknown gene:

options.text: is likely to have a similar function

blocks.explanation: Sequence homology gives a clue to function: a gene or protein homologous to one with a known function is likely to have a similar function (7.4).

book_ref.quote: it is likely to have a similar function

blocks.prompt: 43 Homologous genes in model organisms are studied to:
blocks.explanation: Identifying homologous disease genes across species helps understand disease mechanisms; model organisms' homologous genes give insights into human diseases (7.4).

book_ref.quote: Homologous genes in model organisms can be studied to gain insights into human diseases

blocks.prompt: 44 According to structural homology, proteins with similar three-dimensional structures:

options.text: often perform similar functions even if their sequences are not highly similar

blocks.explanation: Structural homology is similarity of 3D structures due to shared ancestry; such proteins often perform similar functions even with dissimilar sequences (7.4).

book_ref.quote: Proteins with similar structures often perform similar functions, even if their sequences are not highly similar

blocks.prompt: 45 Structural homology is crucial in drug design because drugs:

options.text: are made from DNA sequences only
are designed without knowing any protein
are often designed to interact with specific protein structures

blocks.explanation: Drugs are often designed to interact with specific protein structures, so knowing structural relationships helps design more effective drugs (7.4).

book_ref.quote: structural homology is crucial in drug design
